newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais prepare to import 150,000T tariff-free corn.
newsitem.headline: Thais prepare to import 150,000T tariff-free corn.

text.p: Thailand's grains market revived after its baht devaluation blues last week following news on Tuesday that the commerce ministry was set to approve imports of an additional 150,000 tonnes of zero-tariff corn.

A commerce ministry source told Reuters officials were deciding on the timing for the imports. However, it was likely that the import period will be short and that it could force the industry to buy cargoes in transit, he said.
The move was prompted by near-term shortages of corn supplies caused by an unseasonably late rainy season.

Despite improved rainfall recently, the first corn crop in many areas had already been damaged by lack of rain during the crucial tasselling stage of growth in May and June. Thailand had a dry spell between late April and June although the rainy season normally starts in May.
Although most farmers replanted to make up for damaged crops, supplies were not expected to be available until late August instead of early July as anticipated.
"I hope the government will approve it soon. The shortage is real. They should have realised it a while ago," said an executive at a major feed mill.
If the commerce ministry approves the quota, the proposal will have to receive final approval from the cabinet.
Traders said despite the weakening baht which has lost nearly 15 percent since its flotation, the industry would still need to import corn urgently.
"Demand is very strong. Moreover, at current exchange rates, importing corn is a viable choice given the fact that local prices rose above 5.00 baht a kg," said a trader with a major European house.
"And we don't think the central bank will allow the baht to fall below 30 baht per dollar," said the trader.
The central bank on Monday confirmed it intervened to prop up the baht as regional currency woes sent it tumbling below 30 -- a level which the bank indicated was already too low.

In the oilseeds market, one oil crusher was said to have bought 30,000 tonnes of soybeans for August shipment. Around 57,000 tonnes were due to arrive by the end of this month for another vegetable oil company, traders said.
Soymeal was quiet, with only one cargo bought so far over the week, trade sources said. Local prices were stable at 9.80-9.85 baht per kg. --Bangkok newsroom 66-2-652-0642
